name: drawer
purpose: Panel that slides in from a screen edge, built on native <dialog>. Modal drawers use showModal() (top layer, inert background, backdrop, scroll lock, focus restoration); non-modal drawers use show() and keep the page interactive. Close reasons and cancelable close events match Dialog.
whenToUse: Secondary tasks that keep page context visible, such as editing a record from a list.
Navigation or settings panels on small screens (modal).
Supplementary panels such as filters or details next to live content (non-modal).
whenNotToUse: Short confirmations or destructive prompts: use Dialog (role=alertdialog).
Primary page content or long multi-step flows: use a page.
Content anchored to a trigger: use a popover or menu.
Non-modal drawers for tasks that must be completed before continuing: use a modal drawer.
responsive: Side drawers use min(drawer-width token, 100vw) inline size and full viewport block size; top/bottom drawers use full inline size and max-block-size min(drawer-width token, 85dvh). Below 480px, side drawers take 100vw and footer actions stack full-width.
rtl: placement 'start'/'end' follow the resolved direction: 'start' is the left edge in LTR and the right edge in RTL. The physical edge is exposed as data-aui-side and the element receives dir from configuration. Inner layout uses logical properties.
theme: Surface, border, shadow and backdrop tokens; drawer-width-sm|md|lg for size. Forced-colors mode uses CanvasText borders.
security: Title, description, and string content are rendered as text; never parsed as HTML. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry.

performance.testedScale: One drawer at a time, alongside other overlays arbitrated by the overlay stack.

limitations: Non-modal drawers are not in the top layer; they use z-index 1000 and can be covered by page content with a higher stacking context.
The element's dir attribute follows the configured direction (default 'ltr'), not the document's dir attribute.
Slide animations need @starting-style and transition-behavior: allow-discrete; older browsers open and close without animation.
Initial focus follows the native dialog focusing steps: an action with `autofocus: true`, otherwise the first focusable element (the close button when shown).
unsupported: Switching between modal and non-modal after creation (`modal` is init-only).
Rendering HTML strings as content (pass a Node instead).
antiPatterns: Non-modal drawers for blocking tasks or forms that must be completed.
Leaving closeOnBackdrop enabled for drawers with unsaved input without handling aui-cancel.
Stacking several drawers; reuse one drawer with changing content.

adapters.angular: @absoluteui/angular/drawer: AuiDrawer directive (ng-template[auiDrawer]) with an [open] input; the template is the drawer body.
